body:
## Problem Statement

The owner needs to configure four reusable riding presets without changing or connecting to the wheel. The current laptop and watch editors instead wait for fresh wheel settings, write completed adjustments directly to the wheel, and save each adjustment immediately. This makes Cancel ineffective as a way to discard preset edits and makes the additional Save slot button confusing.

Navigation also conflicts with the intended watch interaction: Settings opens by swiping down but currently closes with a right swipe; right swipes leave the preset editor instead of navigating its fields. Preset Clear buttons introduce an unwanted operation. New installations currently contain unconfigured placeholders instead of the owner's four useful starting presets.

This specification is an amendment to #17. It supersedes the fresh-wheel preset editor, direct editor writes, immediate per-field persistence, preset-clearing UI and conflicting navigation specified by #41 and #42. The owner confirmed the replacement interaction after reviewing the implemented editor.

## Solution

Provide the same local preset editor in the laptop's 240×240 staging interface and the dedicated watch application. Settings → Presets selects one of four named presets. Opening loads that preset's saved local definition immediately, including while disconnected. Changes remain in a preset draft. Save validates and stores the entire selected preset, then returns to preset selection. Cancel, or swipe up from the editor, discards the entire draft and returns to preset selection. Editing and saving never send a wheel-setting command.

Swipe down opens Settings from the riding dashboard. Swipe up returns one level through editor → preset selection → Settings → riding dashboard. In the editor, left/right swipes navigate Name → Pedal sensitivity → Dynamic assist → Pedal dip compensation, wrapping in both directions. Navigation retains draft input, including while a keypad is open. Save and Cancel retain their whole-editor meanings on every page and during text/numeric entry. Remove Save slot, separate Set/Done completion, the editor Back button and the preset Clear buttons.

Both applications initially provide these four configured, editable custom presets. Values are percentages:

| Fixed slot | Initial name | Dynamic assist | Pedal sensitivity | Saved Pedal dip compensation | Include dip when applied |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Jump | 0 | 0 | 0 | No |
| 2 | Forest | 0 | 70 | 0 | No |
| 3 | Road | 25 | 30 | 10 | No |
| 4 | Drag | 70 | 20 | 5 | No |

These are editable defaults, not immutable modes. Initialize new configuration and previously unconfigured slots from the corresponding defaults. Preserve existing configured custom presets. Dip omission is an independent choice: its value remains saved and editable while omitted, and applying an omitted dip emits no dip command, including no command to set it to zero.

The separate riding preset menu continues to apply a saved preset immediately with one tap, subject to its existing eligibility and serialized operation rules. Saving a definition and confirming its application to the wheel remain distinct.

## User Stories

1. As a rider, I want Jump, Forest, Road and Drag available initially in both applications, so that I can begin with my chosen preset values.
2. As a rider, I want all four defaults to be editable custom presets, so that I can rename and tune each one for my own use.
3. As a rider, I want my existing configured presets retained during updates, so that new defaults do not overwrite my previous work.
4. As a rider, I want previously unconfigured slots populated with their corresponding defaults, so that all four positions are usable.
5. As a rider, I want a preset editor to open its saved local values without a wheel connection, so that I can prepare presets anywhere.
6. As a rider, I want external wheel changes and incoming telemetry to leave my preset draft alone, so that preset definitions remain under my control.
7. As a rider, I want typing, navigation, inclusion changes, Save and Cancel to emit no wheel-setting command, so that configuration cannot unexpectedly change the ride.
8. As a rider, I want to edit names with usable watch-sized text input, so that I can recognize each preset without a desktop shortcut.
9. As a rider, I want to enter whole percentages for Pedal sensitivity, Dynamic assist and saved Pedal dip compensation, so that I can enter the intended values accurately.
10. As a rider, I want dip inclusion to be separate from its saved value, so that omitting dip does not erase the value I may use later.
11. As a rider, I want all four defaults to start with dip omitted, so that their first application preserves the wheel's current dip setting.
12. As a rider, I want an included dip value of zero to be distinct from omission, so that zero can be applied deliberately.
13. As a rider, I want swipe up to close the Settings view opened by swipe down, so that the navigation follows the direction I expect.
14. As a rider, I want upward navigation to return one level at a time, so that I can move from editing back to the preset list, Settings and dashboard predictably.
15. As a rider, I want left/right swipes to move through the four editor fields and wrap around, so that I can reach every field without leaving the editor.
16. As a rider, I want draft values and unfinished input retained while moving between fields, so that navigation does not discard my edits or commit them prematurely.
17. As a rider, I want Save to include every field and the active keypad's latest input, so that I do not need a separate Set or Done step.
18. As a rider, I want successful Save to return to preset selection, so that completion has a clear result.
19. As a rider, I want Cancel to discard all changes in the current editor and return to preset selection, so that the previously saved preset remains intact.
20. As a rider, I want swipe up from the editor to discard its unsaved draft just like Cancel, so that there is no hidden save on leaving.
21. As a rider, I want the editor completion actions to be Save and Cancel and the preset list to have no Clear buttons, so that the interface presents the operations I need.
22. As a rider, I want invalid input to identify the problem and keep my draft open, so that I can correct it without losing other field edits.
23. As a rider, I want a failed save to preserve the previous usable configuration and my open draft, so that I can retry without rebuilding the preset.
24. As a rider, I want successful saves to survive restart, so that the app and watch remember my presets independently.
25. As a rider, I want failed or interrupted writes to retain a last-known-good recovery path, so that a storage failure does not replace my custom presets with defaults.
26. As a rider, I want existing backup/import/restore behavior to preserve dip values and inclusion choices, so that local backups retain the meaning of my presets.
27. As a rider, I want saving one preset to preserve the other three presets and my alert preferences, so that unrelated settings are not overwritten.
28. As a rider, I want browser reloads, duplicate requests, wheel reconnections and application restarts to avoid implicit saves or wheel commands, so that old interactions cannot repeat themselves.
29. As a rider, I want a saved preset to apply immediately from the riding preset menu, so that editing does not add a new Apply step or confirmation dialog to riding controls.
30. As a rider, I want only the saved preset's included riding settings submitted, so that a draft or omitted dip cannot affect a preset application.
31. As a rider, I want requested, submitted and freshly confirmed preset results to remain distinct, so that a local save or transport receipt is never presented as a confirmed wheel change.
32. As a rider, I want preset application failures, partial results, timeouts and disconnects to remain bounded and visible, so that simplifying editing does not weaken the existing riding controls.
33. As a rider, I want wake/button/recovery behavior and independent alert editing retained, so that the revised preset interface fits the rest of the watch experience.
34. As a rider, I want the same actions to produce matching results in the laptop interface and watch runtime, so that the laptop remains a useful staging prototype.
35. As an owner reviewing the application, I want reproducible input, rendering, packet and storage evidence with explicit provenance, so that offline results can be assessed separately from actual-watch acceptance.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Authority and scope.** The confirmed local-preset decision supersedes the editor model in #41/#42 and the corresponding fresh-wheel editor clauses in #17 and its acceptance milestones. It does not revive laptop/watch configuration synchronization. Each environment owns its own configuration. The corrected scope applies to both implementations, their public action contracts, UI, documentation and active acceptance scenarios.

- **Local draft boundary.** Replace the session-bound wheel editor with one transient draft for the selected fixed slot. Open from saved configuration; name, percentage and dip-inclusion input only change the draft. There is no wheel-read wait, editor readback timeout, editor command attempt or editor wheel-confirmation state. Connection changes and incoming wheel settings cannot seed, replace or terminate this local draft. Respect existing awake/recovery and controlling-UI access rules without requiring a fresh wheel connection. Local editing remains possible in idle, disconnected, simulator and replay contexts; replay remains unable to send wheel commands.

- **Whole-editor Save and Cancel.** Save gathers all fields, including the currently open text/numeric input, validates the complete selected preset, and commits one replacement of that slot through the existing configuration store. Publish the new saved configuration and return to preset selection only after save succeeds. Cancel and upward exit discard the whole draft without changing saved values or their revision. Both meanings apply while the keypad is open. A completed Save closes that editor operation; duplicate or delayed completions cannot reapply its draft. Application restart restores saved definitions, not draft/input/page state or pending commands. Existing browser ownership and stale-request protections remain effective.

- **Validation.** Preserve the established name contract of 1–24 readable characters with non-whitespace content and whole percentages from 0 through 100. Save requires valid name, Pedal sensitivity, Dynamic assist and retained dip value, plus an explicit dip-inclusion choice. Intermediate empty or unfinished numeric input may remain in the draft while navigating, but cannot be saved. Validation failure keeps the draft open and identifies the field requiring correction. There is no per-field persistence or wheel command on accepting input. Preserve text entry, case, spaces, digits, backspace and input-clearing capabilities; clearing characters is separate from the removed operation that unconfigures a preset.

- **Navigation and presentation.** Carry actual pointer/touch recognition through both application routes. Down from the dashboard opens Settings; up follows the Settings hierarchy, specifically editor → preset selection → Settings → dashboard. Up inside the preset editor, including its input view, behaves as whole-editor Cancel. Right is no longer the back gesture along this preset Settings path. Within the editor, left advances and right reverses through Name, Pedal sensitivity, Dynamic assist and Pedal dip compensation, wrapping at both ends and retaining all draft text. Editor field navigation still works while text/numeric input is open; any character-page controls must not consume those gestures as a different operation. Keep Save and Cancel available as the two editor completion actions. Remove the preset-list Clear targets and editor Back, Save slot, preset Clear and separate Set/Done completion targets. Keep all entry and feedback usable within 240×240. Preserve the separate riding preset menu's existing entry/return and immediate-application interaction, and independent alert behavior; update Settings back gestures and instructions consistently wherever they share that hierarchy.

- **Editable defaults.** The table in Solution is the complete initial configuration for the four fixed preset slots on both laptop and watch. They begin configured. The names and values can subsequently be changed through the same editor as any other custom preset. Defaults initialize absent configuration or individual legacy unconfigured slots; they never reset valid configured custom slots merely because the application starts or updates. Road uses fixed documented values of assist 25, sensitivity 30 and dip 10, not a current read from the wheel.

- **Dip value and inclusion.** Persist a valid numeric dip value independently of whether dip is included in preset application. Toggling omission never deletes or resets that value. A draft may edit the remembered value while omitted. Inclusion/omission remains part of the same Save/Cancel transaction. Every initial preset has inclusion off, including Drag with saved dip 5 and Road with saved dip 10. The command boundary must select included fields explicitly; it cannot infer inclusion solely from the presence of a stored numeric value. An included zero generates the existing zero-valued dip command; an omitted zero or nonzero value generates no dip command.

- **Versioned configuration compatibility.** Introduce a versioned configuration representation that can express both saved dip and inclusion, with explicit migration from the existing schema-1 representation. Preserve fixed identities, existing configured names, required riding values, independent alert preferences and saved dip values. A legacy configured preset with a dip field retains that value and inclusion on, including a value of zero. A legacy configured preset without a dip field retains omission; initialize only its previously absent remembered dip value from the default for that fixed slot, without changing its name, sensitivity or assist. A legacy unconfigured slot becomes the complete corresponding default from the table. Migration must be deterministic and idempotent, must not perform wheel I/O, and must not reinitialize valid custom content on subsequent loads. Unknown schemas or invalid configuration receive explicit validation/recovery handling rather than a guessed migration or silent overwrite with defaults.

- **Storage and backup integration.** Apply the same configuration meaning to laptop durable storage, watch native Storage, recovery copies and the existing local backup/export/import/restore path. Known legacy backups remain reviewable and restorable through the same migration. New exports preserve remembered dip even when omitted, and omit telemetry, live wheel settings, draft state, queued commands and confirmation. Preserve revision guards on reviewed replacement so stale previews cannot overwrite newer saves. Migration and saving must preserve a recoverable previous-good copy until replacement is validated; a valid legacy recovery copy must remain usable during transition. Retain bounded size validation, staging/readback validation and visible recovery warnings. Do not claim physical flash atomicity from offline results.

- **Save failure and concurrent configuration changes.** A refused or failed save leaves the active configuration at its last successfully committed state, retains the draft and gives a visible reason with a local retry. An interrupted write must leave a usable validated recovery route, including first-save/default and legacy-migration cases. Retrying saves the complete draft once and never invokes the wheel writer. If configuration is replaced or reloaded while an editor is open, prevent the old draft from silently overwriting newer saved content; require an explicit fresh editor operation rather than replaying stale completion. Saving one slot must compose with the current other slots and alert preferences rather than restoring an old whole-configuration snapshot.

- **Separate preset application.** Keep the existing command encoder, direct transport, serialized preset control and one-tap riding-menu application. Build an immutable request from the saved selected slot, filtering dip by inclusion and excluding local metadata. Preserve current eligibility, including supported use during riding; this revision introduces no stopped-only restriction. Only one preset operation is active; extra taps do not queue. Preserve the five-second submission bound, existing native chunk deadlines, ten-second post-submission confirmation bound, two matching fresh current-session settings frames for all included fields, and explicit failed/partial/unknown outcomes. Preserve session/revision binding, stopped-unsent-write behavior, current-confirmation invalidation and no automatic rollback/retry/reconnect replay. Local editing must not dispatch an operation; committing a configuration change retains the existing revision-based invalidation of outstanding or confirmed preset requests. A saved preset is never labelled wheel-confirmed merely because it was saved.

- **Application integration.** Update the local configuration/backup model, preset draft and application actions, laptop view/input contract, native watch input/control targets/rendering and the projection from saved presets into wheel application. Remove or retire the former editor-specific wheel-writing path so stale UI actions cannot re-enter it. Preserve the existing alert, dashboard, connection, recording/replay, button/horn, sleep/wake and independent recovery responsibilities. The watch implementation retains its established ES5/runtime compatibility and versioned module/bundle conventions.

## Testing Decisions

- **Existing seams, already agreed in this session.** Use the public application action/raw-notification/observable-view/command-output boundary as the primary behavior seam in both implementations. Use the built laptop UI/backend and production watch main/touch/render/native Storage runtime boundaries for integration evidence. These are the existing boundaries the owner approved; no new private-module testing seam is required. Exercise storage persistence through save/load/restart and recovery behavior, and observe the native Storage and transport effects at those external adapter boundaries.

- **What makes a good test.** Assert rider-visible behavior, saved definitions after restart, rendered controls, and outgoing packets using explicit inputs and independent expected values. Do not test private helpers, recompute expected results from the implementation under test, or treat mocks of application modules as integration evidence. Use real application/parser/store/transport code with controlled clock, file/flash, BLE and physical-input boundaries. Prefer focused vertical slices during implementation, then the complete relevant regression checks.

- **Prior art.** Reuse the existing four-slot application/HTTP editor scenarios, built Canvas pointer and browser lifecycle flows, local configuration and backup/recovery tests, raw-frame preset-control traces, and production watch runtime harness. The watch harness already executes touch interrupts, Graphics operations, GATT chunk submission, native Storage failures and independent recovery. Replace the obsolete editor expectations and input sequence with reusable action/frame scenarios for this revision. Retain older evidence with its original provenance, clearly marked as the previous interaction.

- **Initial state and migration.** Assert all four exact table entries on a fresh laptop and watch, all configured and all dip inclusion off. Rename and change defaults, restart, and prove the edits remain. Exercise mixed legacy configuration with configured custom presets, missing dip, included zero/nonzero dip, unconfigured slots and nondefault alerts. Verify exact migration semantics, backup recovery, repeated-load idempotence, compatible updates and that unknown/corrupt inputs are not silently treated as new installs. Include the previous-good recovery copy as the only valid legacy copy and interrupted migration/save cases.

- **All-four local editor behavior.** Open, rename and change every preset without any wheel connection; save and reload the selected slot while checking the other three and alerts. Across open, typing, inclusion toggle, page navigation, Save, invalid Save, failed Save, retry and Cancel, assert zero wheel-setting packets and no implicit scan/read requirement. Feed changing current-session, corrupt, cached and old-session settings while a draft is open and prove they cannot alter its local contents. Disconnect/reconnect must not make the local editor unavailable or turn editing into a control operation.

- **Actual navigation and input.** Drive real down/up gestures through the laptop UI and native touch adapter, including a full editor → list → Settings → dashboard return. Drive left/right wrapping from both end pages, including while the keypad is open, and prove no unintended exit or lost input. Enter names and numbers using on-screen controls for all slots, save directly from the active input screen, cancel and exit upward with unsaved changes, and verify the resulting rendered screen and saved content. Assert that obsolete preset Clear and per-field completion targets are absent or inactive. Exercise invalid/unfinished input, local save failure and retry feedback within the 240×240 surface.

- **Dip semantics.** Exercise changing a stored omitted dip, Save/restart, then include it and apply the saved preset. Verify the remembered value survives each transition. Apply each initial default and assert the exact sensitivity/assist packets with no dip packet. Separately verify included dip zero and included nonzero values. Omission must preserve a simulated wheel's different dip value rather than send zero. Editing a draft must not change what the riding menu would apply until Save succeeds.

- **Durability and lifecycle.** Exercise refused staging, partial/interrupted active writes, valid backup recovery, failed first save, migration recovery, and local backup/import/export/restore through the public application/runtime boundary. A failed Save retains the draft and previous active values; retry produces one successful local commit without a wheel operation. Restart restores saved values without drafts, pending commands or confirmation. Preserve browser owner/read-only behavior and duplicate/stale completion handling. A save that changes configuration while a preset application is pending must preserve existing revision invalidation and stop unsent continuation.

- **Application regression.** Retain immediate one-tap preset application, fresh-session command eligibility, serialized native chunking, all-included-field confirmation, mismatch/timeout/partial/disconnect outcomes, and late-callback/reconnect non-replay checks. Preserve alert editing and persistence, wake-only sleeping button cycles, eligible horn requests, prolonged-hold recovery, dashboard freshness and read-only replay. Separate local editor checks from the wheel-originated readbacks still required to confirm an actual preset application.

- **Matching evidence and bundle rehearsal.** Run the revised reusable action/frame scenarios through both the actual built laptop UI/backend and the production watch application's offline runtime. Retain exact inputs, expected/observed saved states, renderings, outgoing packets, Storage effects, source versions/hashes and simulated-hardware labels. Build, verify and rehearse a complete versioned watch bundle containing the revision; demonstrate compatible configuration load and independent recovery in the offline runtime. Run focused checks and typechecking during implementation and the complete repository checks, including browser flows, at completion. Real display/input/vibration, physical memory fit, live controls and deployment remain under their existing separate milestones.

## Out of Scope

- Expanding or reordering the four fixed slots, immutable named riding modes, new factory-reset or preset-deletion UI, or replacing valid configured custom presets with defaults.
- Reading wheel settings to seed the editor, automatically importing external wheel changes into a preset, or writing wheel settings from any editing/Save/Cancel action.
- Laptop/watch configuration synchronization, shared-base reconciliation, or configuration transfer between the two environments.
- Changing wheel command mappings, alert patterns, riding eligibility, the physical button/horn contract, or the separate riding preset menu's immediate application interaction.
- Persisting unsaved drafts across application restart, replaying earlier commands, or restoring live wheel confirmation from configuration.
- Live wheel experiments, horn operation, watch deployment, firmware/SoftDevice/bootloader changes, or completing actual-device acceptance as part of this specification or its offline implementation.

## Further Notes

- **Source documents:** this specification synthesizes `docs/design/preset-editor-interaction.md`, uses the vocabulary in `CONTEXT.md`, and follows `docs/adr/0002-local-preset-editing.md` as the agreed domain decision.
- **Parent and precedence:** this is a focused replacement specification under #17. On preset editor behavior, navigation, defaults and associated acceptance expectations, it takes precedence over the conflicting clauses in #17, #41 and #42. The fresh-wheel open/readback gates and direct editor write/confirmation scenarios in #41/#42 are explicitly superseded, not additional requirements to retain. Their independent preset-application, durable-storage, runtime and recovery work remains reusable where consistent with this specification.
- **Owner decision:** the confirmed interaction and ADR 0002, “Keep preset editing separate from wheel application,” establish the distinction between a preset draft, a saved riding preset and a confirmed riding preset. ADR 0001's wheel-owned editor is historical. The owner supplied the four defaults and explicitly confirmed that both applications should initially contain them as editable custom presets, with configured custom presets preserved on update.
- **Road provenance:** the retained owner verification summary dated 2026-10-07 records final restored settings of Pedal sensitivity 30, Dynamic assist 25 and Pedal dip compensation 10. Temporary test values 31/26/11 are not the baseline. Road's defaults use the recorded values; they make no claim about the wheel's current live state or full-range hardware acceptance.
- **Acceptance continuity:** update the affected editor expectations in laptop acceptance #31 and actual-watch acceptance #38 when implementing this revision. Preserve the separate deployment/recovery gate #37 and outstanding wheel evidence #9. The ready-for-agent label describes a specified software change and does not grant hardware authorization.
- **Handoff:** split implementation into self-contained tickets with explicit dependencies if needed. No additional owner design interview is required for this confirmed scope. Publish only sanitized summaries, source references and reproducible evidence; private raw recordings, backups and imported community archives remain outside issue-tracker content.
title: Local preset editing, navigation and editable defaults for laptop and watch
